archetypes.name: wire-contracts
archetypes.rationale: A sh-to-Python migration of this scale lives or dies on exact wire-contract preservation: KV key names and ordering, TSV column order, NDJSON field sets, exit codes, and TAB-separated failure rows are all caller-parsed. Even a single renamed or reordered key can break orchestration silently.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every domain migrated (audit-runs, release, combine-issues, verify-main, plugin read-version), check whether the Python implementation emits KV keys in exactly the documented order and with the documented names. Pay special attention to: `resolve-prs` six-key stdout order (IMPLICIT_SINCE_LAST_AUDIT, PRIOR_REPORT_NUMBER, PR_LIST, PR_COUNT, RESOLVED_ECHO, ERROR); `close-priors` TAB-separated CLOSE_FAILED rows versus space-separated; `pacific-timestamp` PACIFIC_TIMESTAMP_SOURCE keys and UTC fallback shape; `promote-latest` conditional KV phase sets (pre-selection no-stdout contract, post-selection already-emitted KVs); and `map-runs` no-header TSV column order. Also verify that quiet-routing re-initialization happens before `plugin read-version` emits LARCH_PLUGIN_VERSION so command substitution captures stdout correctly. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: required-file-gating
archetypes.rationale: The _scan_required function in audit_runs.py is a direct port of the multi-condition bash _rf_* condition tree and bail-signal logic — the most complex single piece in this diff, with nested closures and interdependent conditions that are easy to mis-port.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the _scan_required function in python/audit_runs.py against the documented condition tree: empty-steps + bail-signal skip behavior, step9a1 nonempty-without-step9a1 bail path, steps_false short-circuit, and the exn-agg-* conditions. Verify the bail_signal() helper correctly matches only the first non-empty line of final-summary.md against _TERMINAL_RE (not any line). Check that the function returns a tuple only for fatal conditions (registry drift) so the caller's `isinstance(res, tuple)` guard is never accidentally triggered for normal pass/fail outcomes. Also check that the 'always' condition evaluates unconditionally regardless of bail or steps_ran state. Cross-reference test_scan_required_bail_and_step9a1_gating in python/test_audit_runs.py to confirm edge cases are actually covered. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: release-safety
archetypes.rationale: The release_finish.py and promote_release.py modules perform git tag pushes and GitHub release mutations — hard-to-reverse operations whose idempotency and origin-vs-repo coupling guard must fire before any writes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review python/release_finish.py for the origin-vs-repo coupling guard: confirm it runs before fetch, tag, release create/edit, or promote writes (not after). Verify idempotent tag handling: existing correct remote tags are tolerated, mismatched remote tags fail closed, local tag correction is gated on remote tag presence. Check that `release promote` is invoked in-process or via the CLI (not via the retired shell script path) after release create/edit succeeds. In python/promote_release.py, verify promote-latest pre-selection failures emit nothing to stdout and that post-selection failures preserve already-emitted phase KVs. Check that the quiet-mode re-initialization for `plugin read-version` (logging_util.quiet_init before KV emit) is present in python/version_bump.py to prevent command substitution from silently capturing an empty string when LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE is inherited. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
